title: The Garden of Port Alder
premise: Jonah Winterbourne, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and part-time novelist, has spent five years in the coastal town of Port Alder rebuilding her life after a scandal destroyed her legal career — measured out in small, safe steps. When a snowstorm strands her estranged former mentor, Elias Vane, and his rival, maritime lawyer Cora Ashford, at the decommissioned lighthouse where Jonah keeps the light burning, old betrayals resurface alongside an undeniable pull between Jonah and Cora. As evidence emerges that the case which ruined Jonah was built on Elias's perjury, she must choose between reclaiming the career that once defined her by testifying against him, or protecting the fragile new identity she has built with Cora at her side. In the end, Jonah chooses neither the law nor silence but a third path: she tells the truth on her own terms, loses the restoration of her name, and gains something better — a home, a love that sees her clearly, and a garden planted where the light used to reach.
about_author: Wendell Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering courthouses and coastlines before turning to fiction. The author lives beside a working lighthouse and writes each morning before the fog lifts.

chapters.title: The Light That Keeps Me
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Five years after fleeing her disgraced legal career, Jonah tends the decommissioned Port Alder lighthouse and writes novels no one knows are hers. Her ordered life of small safe steps is established — until a letter arrives announcing the lighthouse's final decommission sale. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine comfort.

chapters.title: Two Cars in the Snow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A freak October snowstorm strands two travelers on the coastal road: Elias Vane, the mentor whose testimony once shielded himself and condemned Jonah, and Cora Ashford, his courtroom rival who once believed Jonah guilty. With the ferry cancelled, Jonah has no choice but to shelter them both at the lighthouse. Emotional beat: trapped proximity, old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: What the Fog Remembers
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Confined by the storm, Cora watches Jonah move through the lighthouse and realizes the woman she helped destroy bears no resemblance to the person she condemned. A shared pot of tea becomes an interrogation neither can escape. Emotional beat: dawning recognition, guilt sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Cornered by memory and whiskey, Elias recalls the case that made all three careers and broke one — and lets slip a detail only the true falsifier could know. Jonah hears it from the stairwell. Emotional beat: confession half-swallowed, the past turning over like a stone.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah confronts what she heard and nearly flees — the old instinct to disappear. Instead she stays, and in the storm's enforced stillness she and Cora talk honestly for the first time, the beginning of something tender and terrifying. Emotional beat: choosing to stay, first fragile intimacy.

chapters.title: The Storm Breaks
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. The roads clear and the spell threatens to break. Cora, back in her city office, pulls the old case file and finds the discrepancy Elias revealed — proof enough to reopen everything, if she's willing to burn her own reputation doing it. Emotional beat: justice versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Elias offers Jonah a deal: his public recantation in exchange for her silence about his perjury — restoring her bar license, her name, the career that saved everything. It is everything she wanted, wrapped around a lie she'd have to live inside. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: The Garden of Port Alder
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jonah shows Cora the wild garden she planted in the lighthouse keeper's old plot — the life she built from nothing. Cora tells her the truth is coming out with or without her testimony, and that she refuses to be saved by another bargain. Emotional beat: love that demands honesty, not protection.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the reopened inquiry, Jonah takes the stand and tells the whole truth — Elias's perjury, her own silence, her own complicity in letting the lie stand. She forfeits any claim to reinstatement. Elias's career collapses; hers does not return. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, release, the cost of a clean conscience.

chapters.title: Where the Light Used to Reach
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Spring comes to Port Alder. The lighthouse is sold to a preservation trust Cora quietly arranged; Jonah's novel publishes under her own name at last. In the garden they planted together, Cora asks what Jonah will do now, and Jonah answers: stay. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely, identity reclaimed, love that sees clearly.
